The goal sets the shape: how heavy, how many sets, how the week is split. It doesn\'t set a number to hit. Logging and the next target do that.
Full-body days at a steady effort
Heavier loads build strength (ACSM 2026). Size comes from enough sets near your limit at any load. For general fitness, WHO 2020 advises strength work on 2 or more days a week.

Two strength days covering the major muscles is the floor in WHO 2020 and ACSM 2026. Past that, how the week is spread barely changes results, so pick what you can keep. Sessions are cut to fit the minutes.
The smallest weight you can add decides whether a lift moves by load or by reps first.
Experience sets the starting effort and how fast loads move. 65 or older keeps more reps in reserve and opens each lifting day with a short balance warm-up. Nothing here is stored as a profile.
Each one is in the plan.
Choosing your own lifts makes training feel better (Oliveira 2015), and in a trial of older adults self-chosen loads built as much strength as assigned ones. Each one you pick is in the plan.
A recent set of 10 reps or fewer and how hard it felt give a starting estimate (Epley). Leave a lift blank and its first session finds the weight.
Each lifting day opens with a short balance warm-up. More balance work on other days helps: WHO advises it on 3 or more days a week from 65.

Doing the main goal first in a session protects it (Eddens 2018). Lifting and running in one session cost some explosive strength; sessions three hours apart showed no such cost (Schumann 2022).

A timed run or a shuttle test
Events differ in how far the long run goes, what the hard sessions are, and how long the taper is. Most training stays easy for all of them.
Running injury in the past year

Experience sets where lifting and running start. A runner whose longest recent run is under 30 minutes and under 5 km starts on a run/walk ladder, as does a New runner who leaves it blank; Racing runners skip it. For a fitness test or a race up to 3000 m, a Some runner skips it after 20 minutes or 2 miles without walk breaks; a New runner still needs 30 minutes or 5 km. A past running injury starts it one level lower. Nothing here is stored as a profile.
The date sets the build and a taper of up to three weeks that cuts volume and keeps intensity (Bosquet 2007). A recent result predicts pace for races up to the marathon (Riegel).
Interval reps aim slightly faster than the target pace. A date tapers the last ten days.

Runs past the run/walk ladder stay within 10% of your longest session in the last 30 days, a limit from runners (Frandsen 2025). This answer stands in for 30 days, or until there\'s a log.
Lifting and running in the same visits
Sessions three hours or more apart showed no cost to explosive strength; the same session did (Schumann 2022). Separate days need more days a week.
